original_question: Let T(a_1, a_2, ..., a_n) be a norm form written in some integral basis of a proper degree-n extension of Q. Determine all functions f: Z -> C such that T(f(a_1), f(a_2), ..., f(a_n)) depends only on the value T(a_1, a_2, ..., a_n), rather than on the specific tuple (a_1, a_2, ..., a_n).
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 6 ("Pseudo-automorphisms of norm forms in number fields").
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended target almost verbatim: a norm form T written in an integral basis of a proper degree-n extension of Q, a function f: Z -> C, and the invariance requirement that T(f(a_1),...,f(a_n)) should depend only on the value of T(a_1,...,a_n), not on the particular tuple.
missing_details: The field data should be fixed explicitly: choose a proper number field K/Q with [K:Q]=n>1 and a fixed integral basis omega_1,...,omega_n of O_K.
The norm form should be defined, not just named: T(a_1,...,a_n)=N_{K/Q}(a_1 omega_1+...+a_n omega_n) for (a_1,...,a_n) in Z^n.
The quantifier should be stated explicitly: the condition is required for all integer tuples (a_1,...,a_n) in Z^n.

The phrase "depends only on the value" should be formalized as the existence of a function h on the value set T(Z^n) (equivalently on Z, since norm forms take integer values on Z^n) such that T(f(a_1),...,f(a_n))=h(T(a_1,...,a_n)) for all tuples.
To be paper-faithful, the question should be phrased as an open classification problem ("characterize all such f") rather than as if the note itself already contains the classification.

The paper's Section 4 immediately distinguishes this general problem from the separate cubic specialization in Problem 7, so the refined question should stay with the general norm-form formulation and not drift to the cubic example.
refined_question: Fix a proper number field K/Q of degree n>1 and an integral basis omega_1,...,omega_n of O_K. Define the associated norm form by T(a_1,...,a_n)=N_{K/Q}(a_1 omega_1+...+a_n omega_n) for (a_1,...,a_n) in Z^n. Characterize all functions f: Z -> C for which there exists a function h: T(Z^n) -> C such that T(f(a_1),f(a_2),...,f(a_n)) = h(T(a_1,a_2,...,a_n)) for every (a_1,...,a_n) in Z^n.
justification: The closest official target is Problem 6 in Section 4: it asks, in essentially the same words, for all functions f: Z -> C such that the norm form evaluated at f(a_1),...,f(a_n) depends only on the original norm-form value. The surrounding paragraph then says that a special norm-form case was solved by U. Zannier, and Problem 7 immediately turns to a specific cubic norm form; this confirms that your draft is aimed at the general Problem 6, not at the narrower cubic example. The main improvement needed is only to make the fixed field K, the integral basis, the definition of the norm form, and the factor-through-T meaning of "depends only on" fully explicit.
